new_entities.name: Screen time above 3 hours daily
aliases: more than 3 hours of daily screen time
new_entities.description: Recreational screen exposure exceeding about three hours per day in adolescents.

new_entities.name: Adolescent mental health
new_entities.description: Mental health and psychological wellbeing outcomes in adolescents.

edges.effect_quant: A 2023 systematic review including 50 studies concluded that most studies linked greater screen exposure with worse adolescent mental health, and a 2021 international observational analysis of 577,475 adolescents found that increasing recreational screen time beyond 2 hours per day was dose-dependently associated with poorer mental wellbeing.
edges.population: adolescents with recreational screen use, including smartphone, television, gaming, and social media exposure
edges.mechanism: Excessive screen time can crowd out sleep, physical activity, in-person interaction, and recovery time while increasing exposure to overstimulation, social comparison, and stress reactivity.
edges.summary: High recreational screen time has a fairly consistent harmful association with adolescent mental wellbeing, especially once exposure rises above a moderate threshold. The effect is not catastrophic at the individual level, but it is strong enough across populations to justify a harmful classification.
edges.caveats: Screen content, context, and displacement effects matter; the relationship is not identical across all screen activities. The evidence is strongest for overall mental wellbeing and internalizing symptoms at higher exposure levels, not for every possible psychiatric outcome.

evidence.citation: Santos RMS et al 2023 BMC Psychol
evidence.notes: The associations between screen time and mental health in adolescents: a systematic review.
